question: DMART is offering Buy 30, get 11 free on grocery items. What is the net percentage discount being offered by DMART? (Correct up to two decimal places)
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In 'Buy X get Y free' offers, the discount is always calculated on the total number of items received.

Discount % = [Free Items ÷ Total Items] × 100

Total Items = 30 (paid) + 11 (free) = 41 items

Discount % = (11 ÷ 41) × 100 = 1100 ÷ 41 ≈ 26.83%

**∴ The correct answer is 26.83%.**
